title: Ethiopian History University Entrance Exam 2018
description: Ethiopian History University Entrance Exam 2018 featuring 100 authentic questions with step-by-step solutions. Designed for Ethiopian national exam mastery.

questions.questionText: Which kingdom to the north of the Gojeb River was defeated by the Oromo and as a result included Limmu in its name?
options: Gojjam
Enarya
Damot
Gonga
questions.explanation: Enarya (Ennarya), located north of the Gojeb River, was defeated and absorbed by the Oromo, leading to the formation of the Limmu-Enarya kingdom.

questions.questionText: What factor helped Imam Ahmed to strengthen the Sultanate of Adal and pose a challenge to the Christian Kingdom?
options: Mobilization of people across the lowlands to fight together against the Christian Kingdom
Inability by the Christian Kingdom to raise effective military forces
The unexpected defeat of Emir Mahfuz by the army of Emperor Libne Dingil
Military support from the Ottoman Turks through the Red Sea
questions.explanation: Imam Ahmed (Gragn) successfully united and mobilized pastoral and lowland peoples across the region under the banner of jihad, forming a powerful force against the Christian Kingdom.

questions.questionText: What was the major attention behind Portuguese and Turkish military support for the Christian Kingdom and the Sultanate of Adal?
options: Their grand plan to colonize the whole Ethiopian region
Their desire to spread their respective religions in Ethiopia
Their desire to dominate the Mediterranean and Red Sea trades
The interest of both powers to control coastal territories
questions.explanation: The external intervention by Portugal and the Ottoman Empire was driven by their broader geopolitical rivalry and desire to control and dominate lucrative regional trade routes, particularly in the Red Sea and Indian Ocean.

questions.questionText: What direction did the Mecha and Tulama branches of the Oromo take during the population movement of the 16th century?
options: Towards central and western Ethiopian region
Northward in the direction of the Rift Valley Lakes
Towards the south of the highland regions of North Kenya
Towards north and the east along the Awash River
questions.explanation: During the 16th-century Oromo population expansion, the Mecha and Tulama branches migrated and settled into the central and western regions of Ethiopia.

questions.questionText: What was the royal clan that held political power in the Kingdom of Kafa from 1390 to the late 19th century?
options: Bushasho
Tigre
Minjo
Mikkerecho
questions.explanation: The Minjo clan constituted the royal dynasty that ruled the Kingdom of Kafa from its founding around 1390 until its incorporation into the modern Ethiopian state in the late 19th century.

questions.questionText: What was the major factor that forced the Christian Kingdom to shift its political center to the north of the Abay River?
options: Threat from the advancing Oromo population movement
Rivalry among royal descendants for power
Defeat in the hands of the Sultanate of Adal
The advance of the Portuguese from the Red Sea
questions.explanation: The pressure and advancement of the Oromo population movement during the 16th century forced the Christian Kingdom to shift its political center northward across the Abay River (into regions like Gondar).

questions.questionText: Which of the following is correct about the nature of Ethiopian contact with Europe during the Zemene Mesafint?
options: Travellers had little or no interest in claiming territory.
Some European envoys signed treaties with regional lords.
The relationship was managed at the royal court only.
Ethiopian rulers were interested in religious alliance.
questions.explanation: During the Era of Princes (Zemene Mesafint), due to the decentralization of power and weak central monarchy, various European travelers and envoys engaged and signed agreements/treaties directly with powerful regional lords.

questions.questionText: Which of the following was a social consequence of the Industrial Revolution in Britain?
options: Spread of large scale unemployment
Replacement of women by male workers
The emergence of large urban centers
Decline of tension among classes
questions.explanation: The Industrial Revolution drove rapid urbanization, resulting in the massive growth and emergence of large industrial cities and urban centers around factories.

questions.questionText: What was the common feature of the American War of Independence and the French Revolution of 1789?
options: Neither succeeded in establishing a democratic government.
Neither supported the other during the actual revolution.
Both struggled against repressive foreign colonial rule.
Both were influenced by the ideas of the Enlightenment.
questions.explanation: Both the American and French Revolutions drew profound ideological inspiration from the intellectual concepts and political philosophy of the Enlightenment.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about the consequences of the Congress of Vienna?
options: Affirmation and consolidation of the revolutionary situation
Replacement of royalty by republican regimes
Redrawing the map of Europe to restore former boundaries
Reaffirmation of the new territorial entities
questions.explanation: The Congress of Vienna (1814–1815) sought to restore the balance of power in Europe by redrawing the map and reinstating traditional monarchies and former boundaries prior to the French Revolution and Napoleonic Wars.

questions.questionText: Which of the following political organizations refused to join the Union of Marxist-Leninist Organizations in early 1977?
options: The Revolutionary Flame
The All-Ethiopia Socialist Movement
The Worker's League
The Ethiopian People's Revolutionary Party
questions.explanation: The Ethiopian People's Revolutionary Party (EPRP) fiercely opposed the Derg and refused to join the government-backed Union of Marxist-Leninist Organizations (known as EMALEDH).

questions.questionText: What was the impact of colonialism on post-independence African states?
options: It stimulated rapid industrialization in African continent.
It enabled them to enjoy the fruits of democracy in Africa.
It made them heavily dependent on their former colonial powers.
It motivated them to work hard for economic prosperity.
questions.explanation: Colonial rule left structural economic distortions and unequal ties, leaving newly independent African states heavily dependent on their former colonial powers (neo-colonialism).

questions.questionText: Which of the following was a serious problem of African politics from 1965 to the 1980s?
options: External intervention in the domestic affairs
Widespread military coup d'états
Unprecedented population growth
Lack of ideological support from the global power
questions.explanation: The decades following independence, particularly from the mid-1960s through the 1980s, were plagued by severe political instability characterized by frequent and widespread military coups d'état.

questions.questionText: What was the colonial legacy that precipitated economic crises in independent Africa?
options: Dependence on agriculture
Reliance on single commodity export
Diversification of export items
Exhaustion of natural resources
questions.explanation: Colonial economic policies tied African colonies to the production and export of one or a few primary agricultural or mineral commodities, making them highly vulnerable to global price fluctuations and economic crises.

questions.questionText: What was the major impact of the involvement of the superpowers in post-independence Africa? They
options: worked towards resolving internal political conflicts peacefully.
refrained from providing weapons during interstate wars.
allowed nationalism to take its own course.
created ideological division among African states.
questions.explanation: During the Cold War, superpower competition introduced deep ideological divisions and proxy conflicts among African states, heavily influencing continental politics.

questions.questionText: Which of the following events took place during the Transitional Government of Ethiopia between 1991 and 1995?
options: An interim government charter was established.
Arbitrary administration was established.
The existing fourteen provinces were kept intact.
The former armed' forces were integrated with the new.
questions.explanation: During the Transitional Period (1991–1995), a Transitional Charter of Ethiopia was established to serve as the supreme law of the land before the adoption of the 1995 FDRE Constitution.

questions.questionText: Which of the following principles was adopted as a framework agreement for Nile Basin states?
options: Equitable utilization of the water
Adoption of unilateral water treaties
Recognition of the 1959 Agreement
Using force to attain ones interest
questions.explanation: The cooperative framework principles for Nile Basin states heavily emphasize the equitable and reasonable utilization of shared water resources.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a value of indigenous knowledge systems? The fact that
options: it is largely limited to traditional medicine.
it is mainly transmitted by written records.
it is integral to the local cultural complex.
it draws on information external to the locality.
questions.explanation: Indigenous knowledge systems are deeply embedded and integral to the local cultural complex, traditions, and daily practices of a community.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is a characteristic feature of indigenous knowledge?
options: It is replaceable.
It is holistic.
It is universal.
It is fragmented.
questions.explanation: Indigenous knowledge is typically characterized as being holistic, as it integrates social, ecological, spiritual, and economic dimensions of life.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the value of heritages? It
options: helps to encourage patriotism.
tends to encourage differences.
helps anticipate the future.
builds on memories of individuals.
questions.explanation: Cultural and historical heritages foster a sense of national identity, shared belonging, and patriotism among citizens.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is correct about the value of studying history?
options: It helps people understand their societies in a critical way.
It enables people to justify their actions in the present.
It helps communities to feel superior to other communities.
It enables states to control their populations easily.
questions.explanation: Studying history develops critical thinking by helping individuals analyze past events, societal developments, and how societies have evolved over time.

questions.questionText: What is the theory that links human origin to a supernatural force?
options: Relativist
Absolutist
Evolutionist
Creationist
questions.explanation: The creationist theory posits that life and human beings were created by divine or supernatural agency.

questions.questionText: What is the argument of state formation at the core of the theory of 'oriental despotism'?
options: Economic leaders enabled chiefs along trade route to be kings.
Leaders of irrigation-based agriculture become powerful kings.
Religious leaders became kings as representatives of God on earth.
Military leaders promoted warriors to the position of kingship.
questions.explanation: The theory of oriental despotism argues that large-scale irrigation and hydraulic agricultural systems required centralized management and control, leading to the rise of powerful autocratic rulers and kings.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is correct about the Nile River and Egypt? The river
options: caused huge damages due to seasonal flooding.
permanently separated eastern and western regions.
exposed Egypt to frequent foreign invasions.
enabled Egypt to be politically united.
questions.explanation: The Nile River served as a vital unifying geographic and economic corridor that facilitated communication, transport, and political unity throughout ancient Egypt.

questions.questionText: Which of the following was an achievement of ancient Indian civilization?
options: Erection of Ziggurat or Tower of Babel
Production of vases in porcelain technology
Building pyramids for kings
Use of furnace-baked bricks
questions.explanation: Ancient Indian civilization (such as the Indus Valley Civilization) is well-known for its advanced urban planning and the extensive use of standardized furnace-baked bricks.

questions.questionText: Which of the following Afro-Asiatic families of languages is NOT spoken in Ethiopia?
options: Semitic
Cushitic
Berber
Omotic
questions.explanation: Berber is a branch of the Afro-Asiatic language family predominantly spoken in North Africa, whereas Semitic, Cushitic, and Omotic are major language families spoken in Ethiopia.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following was the earliest creature gradually evolving into the genus Homo?
options: Pongidae
Australopithecus
Gorilla
Chimpanzee
questions.explanation: Australopithecus is widely recognized in paleoanthropology as the key early hominin genus that eventually gave rise to the genus Homo.

questions.questionText: Which of the following features is correct about the Sultanate of Shewa?
options: It successfully defeated the rival kingdom of Damot.
It was overthrown by the Walasma Dynasty of Ifat.
It had cordial relationship with the Zagwe Dynasty.
Its capital was located in what is today Northern Shewa.
questions.explanation: The Sultanate of Shewa was overthrown by the Walasma dynasty of Ifat in 1285 AD, marking the end of the Makhzumite dynasty and the Sultanate of Shewa.

questions.questionText: Which of the following empires dominated the Eastern part of Europe between the 5th and 15th centuries?
options: The Greek
The Russian
The Roman
The Byzantine
questions.explanation: The Byzantine Empire dominated the eastern part of Europe throughout the medieval period (between the 5th and 15th centuries).

questions.questionText: What was a major achievement of the Tang dynasty (618-907) AD in Medieval China?
options: Introducing Neo-Confucianism as a state philosophy
Becoming the first dynasty in China to invent the magnetic compass
Building Chang'an as the largest city in the world
Rebuilding the Grand Canal linking Yangtze and Chang Rivers
questions.explanation: Building Chang'an as the largest planned urban center and metropolis in the world was a notable characteristic and achievement during the height of the Tang dynasty.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is correct about the expansion of the Ottoman Turks? They
options: failed to conquer much of the nations in the Balkan Peninsula.
effectively repulsed European pressure during the Crusade.
succeeded to capture Vienna, the capital of Austria in Europe.
brought an end to the Byzantine Empire by seizing Constantinople
questions.explanation: A major milestone in the expansion of the Ottoman Empire under Mehmed II was the capture of Constantinople in 1453, which brought an end to the Byzantine Empire.

questions.questionText: What was the 16th-century Reformation in essence? It was a
options: political upheaval.
religious movement.
cultural revolution.
technological transformation.
questions.explanation: The 16th-century Reformation was fundamentally a major religious movement within Western Christianity that posed a religious and political challenge to the papal authority of the Catholic Church.

questions.questionText: Which of the following peoples formed the social basis and military strength of Imam Ahmed of Adal?
options: The Silte
The Somali
The Oromo
The Sidama
questions.explanation: The Somali peoples, along with other Muslim pastoralist groups in the Horn of Africa, formed a significant social and military base during the conflicts led by Imam Ahmed (Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi) of the Adal Sultanate.

questions.questionText: Which of the following was a consequence of the Oromo population movement?
options: The consolidation of the Muslim Sultanate of Adal
The advancement in using Amharic as the state language
The transition of Oromo people to sedentary farming
The destruction of Jegol the wall around a city of Harar
questions.explanation: Over time and through interactions in different regions, many Oromo communities integrated into local administrative systems and transitioned toward sedentary farming and mixed agriculture.

questions.questionText: What was the motive of Emperor Susenyos in declaring Catholicism as a state religion in place of Orthodox Christianity?
options: He needed Portuguese military support to consolidate his power.
He believed Orthodox Christianity was an obstacle to change.
He sought European support to get access to the Red Sea as an outlet.
He thought Catholicism properly reflects the dogma of Christianity.
questions.explanation: Emperor Susenyos converted to Catholicism and declared it the state religion primarily because he hoped to secure Portuguese and European military assistance to suppress rebellions and consolidate his royal power.

questions.questionText: Who was marked the beginning of the period known as the Zemene Mesafint in Ethiopian history?
options: Ras Gugsa Wolle
Ras Kasa Mircha
Ras Ali II
Ras Michael Sehul
questions.explanation: The ascension of Ras Michael Sehul of Tigray to great power and his involvement in the political manipulations of the imperial throne marked the formal onset of the Era of the Princes (Zemene Mesafint) in the mid-18th century.

questions.questionText: What was the dynasty that Mutota founded in Zimbabwe in the 15th century?
options: Great Zimbabwe
Zulu
Changamire
Mwene Mutapa
questions.explanation: King Mutota founded the Mwene Mutapa (or Mutapa) dynasty in the 15th century after leaving the region of Great Zimbabwe.

questions.questionText: Why was the Third Phase of the Atlantic slave trade known as free trade? Because
options: Three continents along the Atlantic Ocean participated in the trade.
the trade witnessed the involvement of individual pirates.
increasing involvement of individuals made the competition fierce.
companies monopolized the slave trade with a military support.
questions.explanation: The Third Phase of the Atlantic slave trade is referred to as the period of free trade because monopolies (like the Royal African Company) lost their exclusive rights, allowing private traders and independent merchants to enter the trade, intensifying competition.

questions.questionText: What was the general idea shared by Enlightenment philosophers in the economic sphere? They
options: supported reduction of imports and enlargement of exports.
supported protective tariffs and growth of import trade.
encouraged mercantile theory and favourable balance of trade.
advocated free trade and limited state intervention in business.
questions.explanation: Enlightenment economic thinkers, such as the Physiocrats and Adam Smith, criticized mercantilism and advocated for free trade, laissez-faire policies, and limited state intervention in business.

questions.questionText: Which of the following was a major cause of the American War of Independence against the British Empire?
options: The use of force to recruit soldiers for war against France
The declaration of American states as part of British continent
The decision by British to stop the import of slaves from Africa
The successive impositions of additional taxes on the people
questions.explanation: The American Revolutionary War was largely triggered by British policies imposing various taxes and duties (such as the Stamp Act and Townshend Acts) on the American colonies without parliamentary representation.

questions.questionText: Which of the following was a feature of capitalism in Europe between the 16th and 17th centuries?
options: Investment on government enterprises
Predominance of mercantilism
Expansion of the service sector
Decline of nation states
questions.explanation: During the 16th and 17th centuries, early capitalism was heavily characterized by mercantilism, where European states heavily regulated trade and commerce to build national wealth.

questions.questionText: What was the relationship between nationalism and World War I? Nationalism
options: advocated isolationism and thus discouraged war.
stimulated a sense of unity and friendship among states that could have gone to war.
reduced tension among states and thus delayed the outbreak of international crisis of the time.
made most people in Europe to support the war.
questions.explanation: Fervent nationalism across Europe fueled mutual rivalries and militarism, generating widespread popular enthusiasm and public support when the war broke out.

questions.questionText: Which of the following was an obstacle to the process of Italian unification?
options: The prevalence of Austria who dominated most provinces
The prevalence of Prussia in the southern Italian provinces
The Congress of Vienna with its conservative outlook
The independent existence of Piedmont-Sardinia kingdom
questions.explanation: Austria's direct and indirect control over large portions of northern Italy (such as Lombardy and Venetia) served as one of the primary obstacles to the unification movement.

questions.questionText: What was the "Eastern Question" in international politics before WWI?
options: The declining influence of Russia over Serbia
The diminishing interest of Europe in the Balkans
The continuous weakening of the power of Ottoman Turkey
Decline in nationalism throughout Eastern Europe
questions.explanation: The 'Eastern Question' referred to the diplomatic and political problems posed by the continuous decay and disintegration of the Ottoman Empire ('the sick man of Europe') and how European powers would handle the resulting vacuum.

questions.questionText: Which of the following ideas describes the French policy of colonial rule in Africa?
options: Assimilation
Divide and Rule
Indirect Rule
"Tribal" distinction
questions.explanation: France's official colonial policy in Africa was historically rooted in assimilation, aiming to spread French culture, language, and values to subject populations.

questions.questionText: In what way did long-distance trade in 19th century Ethiopia contribute to the interaction of peoples?
options: Through the importation of goods from the outside world
By the transaction of humans as commercial goods
By the movement of people and exchange of culture with each other
Through the movement of commercial items across long distances
questions.explanation: Long-distance trade routes brought different ethnic groups, merchants, and communities into contact, facilitating the movement of people and the exchange of culture and ideas.

questions.questionText: What is the symbolism of Gafat in the modernization efforts of Emperor Tewodros II?
options: Establishment of a gun-foundry for mortar manufacturing
Creation of a military academy to form a national army
Imprisonment of European missionaries in the kingdom
Foundation of a capital city as a center of modernity
questions.explanation: Gafat symbolizes Emperor Tewodros II's efforts to introduce modern technology and manufacturing, specifically establishing a gun-foundry to cast modern cannons and weapons.

questions.questionText: What was the effect of the Qelad system introduced in many parts of southern Ethiopia?
options: It increased state revenue from taxing land.
It undermined the privatization of land.
It distributed land to landless people.
It strengthened the tenure rights of local people.
questions.explanation: The Qelad (measuring) system was associated with land measurement and imperial land tenure settlements that altered and undermined indigenous traditional land ownership and privatization or communal patterns.

questions.questionText: In which of the following engagements did Ethiopia gain victory against Italian incursion under the command of Ras Alula Aba Nega?
options: The Battle of Maichew
The Battle of Adwa
The Battle of Dogali
The Battle of Gundet
questions.explanation: Ras Alula Aba Nega commanded Ethiopian forces at the Battle of Dogali in 1887, where they decisively defeated an Italian military column.

questions.questionText: Which of the following was a major factor for the downfall of Lij Iyasu?
options: Attempt to integrate Muslims through religious equity
The abolition of the traditional Leba Shay to detect thieves
The establishment of a municipal police called Terenbulle
Antagonism with neighbour European colonial powers
questions.explanation: Lij Iyasu's foreign policy choices during World War I—specifically aligning closely with the Central Powers (such as the Ottoman Empire) and antagonizing neighboring European colonial powers (Britain, France, and Italy)—were major factors that alarmed both foreign powers and domestic conservative elites, leading to his overthrow.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about pre-history?
options: It focuses on issues after writing was developed.
It helps us understand democratic principles.
It studies the political life of past societies.
It belongs to the discipline of archaeology.
questions.explanation: Pre-history refers to the period of human history before the invention of writing systems, relying heavily on material remains and the discipline of archaeology for its study.

questions.questionText: Which of the following best describes human evolution during the Neolithic Revolution?
options: The production of first stone tools called hand-axes
The reliance of humans on hunting and gathering
The movement of people from highland to lowland
The transition of humans to food production
questions.explanation: The Neolithic Revolution was characterized by the momentous shift from nomadic hunting and gathering to settled agriculture and food production (domestication of plants and animals).

questions.questionText: During which of period did human beings begun to use language?
options: Mesolithic
Monolithic
Palaeolithic
Neolithic
questions.explanation: Early forms of human speech and language development began during the Palaeolithic (Old Stone Age) era alongside the evolution of early humans and tool-making.

questions.questionText: With which of the following ancient African civilization is the production of iron tools associated?
options: Kush
Zimbabwe
Egypt
Carthage
questions.explanation: The ancient kingdom of Kush (particularly centered around Meroë) became a prominent iron-producing and iron-working hub in ancient Africa.

questions.questionText: Which of the following developments made a major contribution to the spread of Christianity in the 4th century AD?
options: The readiness of Christians to die rather than give up
The preaching of the faith by missionaries in distant areas
The split of the religion into Orthodoxy and Catholicism
The harsh persecution of Christians by Emperor Nero
questions.explanation: During the 4th century AD, the official legalization and endorsement of Christianity within the Roman Empire (such as by Constantine) greatly accelerated missionary expansion and the preaching of the faith in wider areas.

questions.questionText: What was the external factor that led to the decline and eventual fall of the Aksumite kingdom?
options: The growing pressure from the Egyptians
The shift of the trade route to the Zeila port
The rise of Muslim Arabs in the Red Sea
The defeat of the Aksumites in South Arabia
questions.explanation: The rise of Muslim Arabs and their control over trade routes in the Red Sea region isolated Aksum economically, cutting off its vital maritime trade networks and contributing significantly to its decline.

questions.questionText: Which of the following was a major achievement of the Arab-Muslim civilization?
options: The complete abandonment of the clan system
Advancing the Arabic to an international language
Adoption of the architectural designs of the Greeks
Destruction of other religions through Jihad wars
questions.explanation: Arab-Muslim civilization expanded the role of Arabic, establishing it as a major international language of science, culture, commerce, and administration across a vast empire.

questions.questionText: With which of the following was the rise of the Zagwe Dynasty directly associated?
options: The close interaction of the Agaws with the Aksumites
The control of the trade with the Sudan via Metemma
The destruction of Aksum by the Beja
The lengthy military conflict against the Aksumites
questions.explanation: The Zagwe dynasty emerged out of the long-standing integration and interaction of the Agaw people with the northern Aksumite culture and political structures.

questions.questionText: What was the leading narrative that Yekuno-Amlak used to justify his rise to power?
options: Accusing the Zagwe rulers for the decline of Aksum
Alleging that the Zagwe rulers were non-Christians
Linking his genealogy to King Solomon via Menilik I
Agitation for the restoration of Orthodox Christianity
questions.explanation: Yekuno-Amlak and the Restoration dynasty legitimized their rule by claiming direct descent from the ancient Aksumite royal line connected to King Solomon and Queen of Sheba.

questions.questionText: Which of the following was a major factor for the emergence of Muslim Sultanates in Ethiopia?
options: The impact of the Oromo population movement
Their location along long-distance trade route
Decline in the power of the Aksumite state
Ottoman Turkish dominance of the Red Sea
questions.explanation: The growth, prosperity, and positioning of Muslim sultanates in the interior and lowlands of the Horn of Africa were heavily tied to their strategic locations along active long-distance trade routes.

questions.questionText: Which of the following empire was disintegrated and finally reduced to a nation-state after the end of the First World War?
options: Ottoman Turkey
Italy
Austria-Hungary
Russia
questions.explanation: The Ottoman Empire was dismantled following WWI, with its core Turkish heartland transformed into the modern nation-state of Turkey under the Treaty of Lausanne.

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is the first African state to get its independence from British colonial rule?
options: Ghana
Egypt
Nigeria
Sudan
questions.explanation: Ghana (formerly the Gold Coast) gained its independence from Britain on March 6, 1957, becoming the first sub-Saharan African nation to achieve independence.

questions.questionText: What was the pretext that the Italians used to invade Ethiopia in 1935-36?
options: The fact that Ethiopia separated colonial territories under Italian rule
The refusal of Ethiopia to apologize for damage at the Battle of Adwa
The unresolved issue of the Walwal incident of 1934
The admission of Ethiopia to the League of Nations in 1923
questions.explanation: Italy used the Walwal incident of December 1934 as a diplomatic and military pretext to launch its invasion of Ethiopia in 1935.

questions.questionText: Why did Britain support Ethiopia's liberation from Italian occupation in 1941? Because
options: the French showed a desire to colonize Ethiopia from Djibouti.
they were greatly interested to restore Emperor Haile Selassie I.
they knew the patriotic resistance in Ethiopia is too strong to suppress.
the Italians had become their enemy after joining the Entente in 1940.
questions.explanation: Italy entered World War II in June 1940 on the side of the Axis powers against Britain, which made Italian East Africa a direct military target for British forces, leading them to support Ethiopian patriotic liberation forces in 1941.

questions.questionText: Which of the following branch of the United Nations Organization has members with a right to veto decisions?
options: The International Court of Justice
The Security Council
The Secretariat
The General Assembly
questions.explanation: The United Nations Security Council consists of permanent and non-permanent members, where the five permanent members hold veto power over substantive resolutions.

questions.questionText: What was the major factor that led to the split of the Pan-African movement in Africa?
options: Opposing outlooks concerning the liberation of African peoples
Divergent views about the relationship with former colonial powers
Differences on the validity of colonial boundaries
Disagreement over the form and content of continental unity
questions.explanation: The Pan-African movement split into competing blocs (such as the Casablanca and Monrovia groups) largely due to disagreements over how to achieve continental unity—whether through immediate political federation or gradual, functional cooperation among sovereign states.

questions.questionText: Which of the following directly contributed to the formation of the Organization of African Unity (OAU)?
options: The increase in the number of independent states of Africa
The willingness of Ethiopia to make Addis Ababa its seat
The beginning of the Cold War after the end of WWII
The strong desire to create the United States of Africa
questions.explanation: The rapid decolonization and increase in the number of newly independent African states in the late 1950s and early 1960s provided the critical mass and momentum needed to establish a unified continental organization in 1963.

questions.questionText: Which of the following had a long-lasting effect on the economic development of post-liberation Ethiopia?
options: The institution of the Gabbar system in the south
The attraction of considerable foreign investors
The increasing privatization of land
The foundation of the Ethiopian Airlines
questions.explanation: The establishment and expansion of Ethiopian Airlines (founded in 1945) played a foundational and enduring role in the modernization, transport, and international economic connectivity of post-liberation Ethiopia.

questions.questionText: What was the effect of the UN resolution on establishing the Federation of Eritrea with Ethiopia?
options: It prompted the introduction of the 1955 Revised Constitution.
It paved the way for a voluntary union of Eritrea with Ethiopia.
It satisfied the interest of unionist and separatists in Eritrea.
It made Ethiopia entertain certain democratic elements.
questions.explanation: The federal arrangement and the subsequent 1955 Revised Constitution introduced certain limited democratic features, a separate Eritrean constitution, and a parliament within the broader framework of the Ethiopian empire.

questions.questionText: Who was the long serving president of Ethiopia before the EPRDF defeated the Derg regime in 1991?
options: Fikre-Selassie Wogderes
Mengistu Haile-Mariam
Aman Mikael Andom
Teferi Banti
questions.explanation: Mengistu Haile-Mariam was the prominent leader and long-serving president of the People's Democratic Republic of Ethiopia (PDRE) until the Derg regime was overthrown in 1991.

questions.questionText: What was the major reason for which eleven states to break away from the United States of America, leading to the Civil War?
options: The decision made by the federal government to end slavery
The differences on the terms of relationship with Britain
The unbearable taxation by the Federal Government
The restrictions imposed on the export of agricultural products
questions.explanation: The American Civil War was fundamentally sparked by the secession of southern states over states' rights and the institution of slavery, particularly following the election of Abraham Lincoln and tensions regarding the expansion or abolition of slavery.

questions.questionText: Which of the following was a common mechanism through which European states established colonial control in Africa?
options: Conversion of missionaries into colonial officials
Extension of European citizenship to Africans chiefs
Persuasion of African elites to accept colonial control
Conversion of protectorates territories to colonies
questions.explanation: A common colonial administrative practice during the Scramble for Africa was the transition and upgrading of initial informal spheres of influence or protectorates into fully administered formal colonies.

questions.questionText: Which of the following regions of Ethiopia was the most important source of export items for long-distance trade during the 19th century?
options: The North-west
The South-west
The North-east
The South-east
questions.explanation: The south-west region of Ethiopia was exceptionally rich in valuable export commodities such as coffee, gold, civet, and ivory, making it the primary economic engine for 19th-century long-distance trade.

questions.questionText: Which of the following local rulers declared himself as emperor following the death of Emperor Tewodros II?
options: Negus Menelik of Shewa
Negus Tekle-Haimanot of Gojjam
Wagshum Gobeze Gebre Medhin of Lasta
Ras Kasa Mircha of Tigrai
questions.explanation: Following the death of Emperor Tewodros II at Magdala, Wagshum Gobeze of Lasta assumed the imperial throne as Emperor Tekle Giyorgis II.

questions.questionText: What was the unintended consequence of the Hewett (Adwa) Treaty for Ethiopia?
options: The ultimate and fatal enmity of the Mahdists
Undermining the position of Ras Alula Engida
Undermining positive relationship with France
Loss of the right of free transit through Massawa
questions.explanation: The Hewett Treaty facilitated the evacuation of Egyptian garrisons through Ethiopian territory, which deeply antagonized the Mahdists in the Sudan and resulted in long-term, fatal enmity and conflict between Ethiopia and the Mahdist state.

questions.questionText: Which of the following was the major consequence of the Adwa victory for Africans' struggle against colonialism?
options: The inspiration of black unity and regeneration of nationalism in the continent
The military support of Menelik for African liberation movements
The downfall of Prime Minister Francesco Crispi in Italy
Signing of boundary treaties between African states and the colonial powers
questions.explanation: The historic Ethiopian victory at Adwa served as a powerful inspiration for black dignity, solidarity, anti-colonial resistance, and early nationalist movements globally and across the African continent.

questions.questionText: Why was Empress Taytu removed from the palace during the power struggle between 1906 and 1913? It was to
options: facilitate Empress Taytu to travel to her birth place.
end her political role and intervention in any governmental activities.
arrange the marriage between Princess Zewditu and Ras Gugsa Wale.
support Lij Iyasu's designation as heir to Emperor Menelik.
questions.explanation: Empress Taytu was forced out of active political influence and removed from central palace power to curb her heavy political intervention during Emperor Menelik II's incapacitation.

questions.questionText: What was the point of agreement among Britain, France and Italy in the Tripartite Treaty of 1906?
options: Collaborating with Dejazmach Teferi Mekonnen
Partitioning Ethiopian territory among themselves
Protecting the territorial integrity of Ethiopia
Supporting Italy's colonial control of Ethiopia
questions.explanation: In the Tripartite Treaty of 1906, Britain, France, and Italy formally agreed to maintain the political and territorial status quo and integrity of Ethiopia while carving out their respective spheres of economic influence.

questions.questionText: What was the major financial reform in Ethiopia that accompanied the rise of Emperor Haile Selassie I to autocracy?
options: Increase in the number of customs posts
Promoting cash payment and discouraging payment in kind
Decentralization of financial institutions
Provision of credits to peasants with cultivable lands
questions.explanation: The consolidation of centralized government authority and the rise of Haile Selassie I's autocracy was accompanied by financial reforms that promoted monetization, encouraging cash payments (such as salaries and taxes) and moving away from payments in kind.

questions.questionText: Which of the following leaders in West Africa conducted armed resistance against advancing French troops for more than a decade?
options: Urabi Pasha
Al Hajj Umar
Samouri Toure
Harry Thuku
questions.explanation: Samouri Toure led a formidable military resistance against French colonial expansion in West Africa for over a decade (from the early 1880s until his capture in 1898).

questions.questionText: Which of the following phenomena contributed to the development of early capitalist relations in Europe in the second half of the 15th century?
options: Peasant rebellions that forced more people to towns
Increase in trade and investment
Equality of citizens before the law
Extensive commercial interaction with the Ottomans
questions.explanation: The expansion of trade, commerce, and monetary investment during the later 15th century laid foundational elements for the growth of early capitalist relations in Europe.

questions.questionText: What was the main idea behind "Legitimate trade" in Africa early in the 19th century?
options: Replacing trade in slaves by agricultural products
Introducing small-scale industries in West Africa
Making the illegal slave trade legal
Allowing Africans to get wealthy
questions.explanation: Following the abolition of the transatlantic slave trade by European powers, 'legitimate trade' was promoted as a system to replace human trafficking with commerce in raw agricultural and natural commodities (such as palm oil and peanuts).

questions.questionText: What is the language super-family that predominantly spoken in southern parts of Africa?
options: The Niger-Congo
The Khoisan
The Afro-Asiatic
The Nilo-Saharan
questions.explanation: The Niger-Congo language family (specifically through its major Bantu branch) is predominantly spoken across the southern, central, and eastern parts of Africa.

questions.questionText: Which of the following was an achievement of Renaissance art?
options: The reproduction of the architecture style developed in the medieval period
The invention of a sculpture style that gave precedence to life
The introduction of religious paintings that were highly decorated
The development of an artistic style that emphasized on a realistic illustration of life
questions.explanation: Renaissance art broke away from medieval formalism by introducing techniques like linear perspective, shading, and anatomical proportion to achieve a realistic illustration of life and human form.

questions.questionText: What was the major historical dynamics that resulted in the marginalization of the Khoi-Khoi in southern African?
options: Their involvement in the Trans-Atlantic slave trade
Their expulsion from the gold fields by the Cape Colony
Their conquest and enslavement by Bantu migrants
Their displacement by the Dutch settlers
questions.explanation: The pastoralist Khoi-Khoi in southern Africa were progressively marginalized, dispossessed of their grazing lands, and displaced following the expansion and settlement of Dutch colonists (Boers) starting from the mid-17th century at the Cape.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is true about state formation in West Africa before the arrival of the Europeans?
options: States were powerful economically and militarily.
They do very little with the Trans-Saharan trade.
There were several large empires.
States were small and primitive.
questions.explanation: Prior to European arrival, West Africa witnessed the rise of several powerful and extensive centralized empires and states (such as Ghana, Mali, and Songhai) built upon rich trade and political organization.

questions.questionText: What was the relationship between the Moroccan Sultanate and the Songhai Empire by the end of the 16th century?
options: The exchange of commodities between the two reached its peak stage
The Moroccan Sultanate collapsed by the Conquest of Songhai Empire
The Songhai Empire sent an expedition to Morocco to control the salt mines
The Moroccan army invaded the Songhai Empire and it was finally disintegrated
questions.explanation: In 1591, a Moroccan army equipped with firearms crossed the Sahara and invaded the Songhai Empire, defeating its forces at the Battle of Tondibi and leading to the political disintegration of the empire.

questions.questionText: What was the distinctive feature of urbanization in the Gondarine period?
options: Adoption of Byzantine architectural styles
Evolution of a large daily market in the city
Development of public parks and bathes
Domination of local trade by Arab merchants
questions.explanation: A key distinctive feature of urbanization during the Gondarine period was the evolution of vibrant, permanent urban centers featuring large daily markets (such as the Guidamo market in Gondar).

questions.questionText: What was the "discovery" by European explorers in Africa that aroused the interest of the Belgian king Leopold II?
options: The Zaire River was navigable.
Lake Victoria was the major source of the White Nile.
The Zambezi River flows from coast to coast.
The Niger River is accessible from the coast.
questions.explanation: Henry Morton Stanley's exploration and tracing of the Congo (Zaire) River and its navigability intensely aroused the colonial ambitions of King Leopold II of Belgium.

questions.questionText: What was the major achievement of the Roman government under Augustus Caesar?
options: The adoption of a law granting freedom to slaves
Extending the right to vote to women and non-citizens
Maintaining lasting peace throughout the empire
The defeat of Carthage, Rome's major imperial rival
questions.explanation: Augustus Caesar inaugurated the Pax Romana (Roman Peace), a long period of relative stability and peace across the Mediterranean world and the Roman Empire.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is correct about the Mensheviks in the Russian Revolution of 1917?
options: They refused to cooperate with the liberals.
They favoured open party membership.
They were majority party.
They organized a centralized hierarchy.
questions.explanation: Unlike the Bolsheviks, the Mensheviks favored a broader, open party membership and a more inclusive approach, collaborating with bourgeois liberals toward a bourgeois-democratic revolution first.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is correct about the Great Economic Depression during the interwar period?
options: The price of manufactured goods declined more than food stuffs.
It facilitated the assuming of power by militarist nations.
It was caused by unrestricted free trade practices of capitalism.
It affected industrial nation's more than non-industrial nations.
questions.explanation: The severe economic instability and political turmoil caused by the Great Depression fostered conditions that enabled extremist and militarist regimes to seize power in nations like Germany, Italy, and Japan.

questions.questionText: Which of the following state formed an alliance with the Axis Powers in 1940?
options: Britain
Poland
Italy
Soviet Union
questions.explanation: Italy formalized its military alliance with Nazi Germany through the Tripartite Pact (along with Japan) in September 1940, solidifying the Axis Powers.

questions.questionText: What was the objective of the Marshal Plan of 1948?
options: quick economic recovery of Europe
Disengagement of USA from European problems
The formation of the European Union
The division of Germany into East and West
questions.explanation: The Marshall Plan (European Recovery Program) of 1948 was initiated by the United States to provide foreign aid to help secure a quick economic recovery in war-torn Western Europe and prevent the spread of communism.

questions.questionText: Which country was responsible for igniting the Korean War of 1950-53?
options: South Korea
North Korea
USA
Soviet Union
questions.explanation: The Korean War began when North Korean forces crossed the 38th parallel and invaded South Korea on June 25, 1950.

questions.questionText: Which of the following events was the final blow in the dissolution of the Communist bloc?
options: Outbreak of a revolution in the Communist states of Eastern Europe
The dismantling of the wall that divided Germany into East and West
Replacement of USSR by Commonwealth of Independent States
Recognition by USSR of the independence of the Baltic State
questions.explanation: The formal dissolution of the Soviet Union and its replacement by the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS) in December 1991 marked the ultimate and final dissolution of the Soviet Communist bloc.

questions.questionText: Which of the following is correct about the 1942 Anglo-Ethiopian Agreement?
options: It underlined the dominant role of the British.
It allowed the Emperor to enjoy real political power.
It helped to replace the British by the Americans.
It restored the Ogaden territories to Ethiopia.
questions.explanation: The 1942 Anglo-Ethiopian Agreement placed severe restrictions on Ethiopia's sovereignty and heavily underlined the dominant political and military control exercised by Great Britain in post-liberation Ethiopia.

questions.questionText: What was the major economic trend of the imperial government towards the end of the monarchy?
options: Expansion of large-scale commercial plantations
Reduction of land taxes for the benefit of peasants
Huge investment in the industrial sector
Expansion of small-scale industries
questions.explanation: During the final decades of the imperial regime (under Haile Selassie), a major economic trend was the active promotion and expansion of commercial agriculture and large-scale mechanized farms, particularly in the Awash Valley and southern regions.

questions.questionText: What was the characteristic feature of the Ethiopian Student Movement starting from the mid-1960s?
options: Passive resistance against Western influence
Advocacy of armed struggle in rural areas
Militant demand for land tenure reform
Demand for better learning facilities
questions.explanation: A defining, militant characteristic of the Ethiopian Student Movement from the mid-1960s onward was its passionate call and demand for radical land reform, famously summarized by the slogan 'Land to the Tiller'.

questions.questionText: What do you understand by the term "creeping coup" in the 1974 Revolution? It characterizes the
options: rivalry for power among members of the Derg
collaboration of teachers with factory workers
swift actions of the army in ousting the emperor
dismantling of the imperial regime slowly
questions.explanation: The term 'creeping coup' refers to the gradual, step-by-step process through which the military (the Derg) systematically dismantled the institutions of the imperial regime and stripped Emperor Haile Selassie of his power before formally deposing him.
